description: s3Dgraphy connections datamodel including edge types with CIDOC-CRM mappings. v1.6.22 (FRASI DEGLI ARCHI, 2026-10-02, decision of E.D. 2026-10-01): `ui_phrase` {as_source, as_target} on the 34 edge types an interface proposes in a menu — the phrase that names a NEW node created linked to an existing one («US above X», «Property of X», «Document for X»). It is EM language, so it lives here and not in a consumer's i18n; the translations are in datamodel_translations.json, section `edge_types` (fields `ui_phrase_as_source` / `ui_phrase_as_target`). See `_ui_phrase_note`. ADDITIVE: no edge, rule or mapping changed. v1.6.21 (PROPRIETA' DIRETTE, 2026-09-28, decision of E.D. revising v1.6.1): has_property.source += EpochNode, GraphNode. Principle: every node that accepts properties receives them DIRECTLY. The sources are now the graph itself (GraphNode), the documents (DocumentNode, RepresentationModelDocNode), every stratigraphic unit (StratigraphicNode, matched by class MRO so SF, RSF, serSU, USD, USN, USNt... are included; the USNt node_type_restriction has scope stratigraphic and does not narrow has_property) and the epochs (EpochNode). v1.6.1 had routed an epoch's absolute_time_start/end through a ParadataNodeGroup because has_property refused an EpochNode (StratiMiner epoch claims degraded to generic_connection). The ParadataNodeGroup (DP-60, E89) is NOT a mandatory passage: it is a grouping, which can be created on the fly, useful to connect something to the whole set of a node's properties (connecting to the group equals connecting to each member PropertyNode) or to one property inside it. Coherence rule (validator, not datamodel): a PropertyNode in the PNG of X (is_in_paradata_nodegroup + X has_paradata_nodegroup PNG) requires X has_property that PropertyNode. has_paradata_nodegroup.source keeps EpochNode. NOT TOUCHED, question for E.D.: the cidoc P43_has_dimension has domain E70 Thing; A8/E31/E73 satisfy it, an E4 Period does not. s3Dgraphy connections datamodel including edge types with CIDOC-CRM mappings. v1.6.20 (UNA GRAFIA SOLA, 2026-09-27): NEW optional field `spelling_of` on an edge entry, naming the canonical entry of which this one is an OLDER SPELLING. Meaning: the SAME relation, the SAME RDF projection, ACCEPTED WHEN READ, NEVER WRITTEN — every writer (importers, exporters, merge, inference, sync) asks the datamodel for the canonical name (connections_loader: canonical_name / is_canonical False / normalize_edge_name) instead of keeping its own list. It is NOT `deprecated`: `deprecated` drops the edge from RDF on export AND import (measured: an is_bonded_to marked deprecated leaves 0 em:bondedTo triples), which is right for has_timebranch that nobody writes and wrong for a spelling pyArchInit writes every day. Set on the two legacy physical bonds: is_bonded_to spelling_of bonded_to, is_physically_equal_to spelling_of equals. em.ttl is unchanged: it already has ONE property per pair (em:bondedTo, em:physicallyEquals) and its `Maps to:` names both spellings. The datamodel is the source of truth for names (docs/SOURCE_OF_TRUTH.md). s3Dgraphy connections datamodel including edge types with CIDOC-CRM mappings. v1.6.18 (CRMem WIRING, 2026-09-24): il prefisso CIDOC-S3D esce dal datamodel. Non era un namespace: era una stringa che _resolve_prefixed non risolve, quindi nessuna tripla veniva emessa da quei campi. Disposizione termine per termine: incompatibleWith -> em:contrastsWith; belongsToAlternative -> em:belongsToAlternative (is_in_timebranch e has_timebranch); hasSymbolicSpatialRepresentation -> em:hasSemanticShape; isPartOfParadataGroup e hasParadataDocumentation RIMOSSI, perche' crm:P106i_forms_part_of e crm:P129i_is_subject_of dicono gia' quello che serve una volta tipizzato il gruppo; has3DRepresentation RIMOSSO sui tre archi di rappresentazione, perche' crm:P138i_has_representation con la co-tipizzazione del target a E36_Visual_Item basta e il '3D' sta nel rdf:type del bersaglio, non nella relazione. INOLTRE contrasts_with perde crm:P15_was_influenced_by: dominio E7_Activity contro un E4_Period, e comunque un'altra proposizione. Esce sulla sola em:contrastsWith. s3Dgraphy connections datamodel including edge types with CIDOC-CRM mappings. v1.6.17 (CIDOC REPAIR, 2026-09-21): a pass over IRIs that do not exist. An undeclared IRI raises no error anywhere — it makes a well-formed triple that no reasoner uses and no query finds — so these were found by parsing the official releases (CIDOC CRM 7.1.3 + Supplement, CRMarchaeo 2.1.1, CRMinf 1.2.1, CRMsci 3.2, CRMdig 5.0, CRMgeo) and checking every term this file cites against them. FIXED: the nine physical-relation edges (abuts, cuts, fills, overlies, bonded_to, is_bonded_to, equals, is_physically_equal_to, generic_connection) moved from AP11_has_physical_relation to AP11_has_physical_relation_to, the name CRMarchaeo has used since 2.0 — the old one exists only in 1.4.1. is_after: crm:P120_occurs_before is not declared in CRM 7.1.3, so crmarchaeo:AP28_occurs_before — already the extension_mapping, and the same proposition — is promoted to `cidoc` and the extension_mapping cleared; rdf_subject=target is UNCHANGED and still right. has_same_time: crm:P114_is_equal_in_time_to undeclared, same promotion of AP22. changed_from: P123_resulted_from -> P123i_resulted_from (the «i» of the inverse was missing). has_geoposition: the crmgeo:Q4 extension_mapping removed, P53 alone being valid and sufficient. THREE PROJECTIONS RAN BACKWARDS, none of them declaring rdf_subject, so the exporter wrote source-first and the proposition came out reversed: is_in_paradata_nodegroup P106_is_composed_of -> P106i_forms_part_of, has_paradata_nodegroup P70_documents -> P129i_is_subject_of (the reason ParadataNodeGroup becomes E89 in the node datamodel), and is_in_activity, where P9_consists_of is removed and NOTHING replaces it: neither P9i (needs an E4 Period as subject) nor P129i (needs an E89 as object; ActivityNodeGroup is E7) holds, and the empty field is a question for E.D., not an omission. Inverse properties were preferred to rdf_subject throughout: one indirection less. ALSO, by decision of E.D.: has_first_epoch and survive_in_epoch both accept FunctionalUnitNodeGroup, so a functional unit carries its own temporal index — the asymmetry with ActivityNodeGroup, which takes the first and never the second, is meant, because an activity is an event and a functional unit is a thing that persists. «CRMs3D» is renamed «CRMem», in components and in referenced_ontology_versions alike: the companion ontology is em.ttl and its namespace is em:, so the old name pointed at nothing anyone could look up. CRMsci moves 3.1 -> 3.2 (latest release). NOT TOUCHED and still open: the seven CIDOC-S3D properties and their extension_mappings, the E36 co-typing on has_representation_model*, and the direction of has_sub_epoch's P10_falls_within, which the repair report of the same day records as a decision for E.D. v1.6.15 (HW1, 2026-09-16): the act of acquisition gets a BODY. NEW dtc_happened_on_device — DTCNode -> DTCDeviceNode, crmdig:L12_happened_on_device — because until today the apparatus was a STRING inside how.acquisition, and a string cannot be asked «what did this machine produce», «which surveys used that scanner», «that lens was distorted, which models are affected». It attaches to the EVENT and not to the input or the output: the three dtc_kinds axes are the FLOW (what went in, what happened, what came out) and a device is what it happened ON — the distinction CRMdig draws between L12 and L10, and the one that makes the three questions askable. It is CONTEXT and carries no dtc_role, so a provenance walk does not enter it (per _dtc_role_note below). It has NO PROV-O projection on purpose: prov:used is taken by dtc_had_input and prov:Agent ranges over things that bear responsibility, which a camera does not — same honesty as the 2026-08-17 note on wasInformedBy. NOTHING IS REMOVED and nothing is narrowed. NOT DONE, and named so it is not forgotten: a rig (a sensor ON a drone) is an assembly of two devices and has no edge yet; the glyph family says it by drawing their connectors touching, which is a picture and not a statement. s3Dgraphy connections datamodel including edge types with CIDOC-CRM mappings. v1.6.14 (EM16-RMNG, 2026-09-10): the RM container becomes a first-class group in the graph. NEW is_in_representation_model_group — membership of a representation model in a RepresentationModelNodeGroup, on the is_in_* tag convention (is_in_activity / is_in_location / is_in_timebranch / is_in_paradata_nodegroup / is_in_functional_unit), 1:1 instead of m:n because a mesh belongs to exactly one container. WIDENED has_representation_model.target += RepresentationModelNodeGroup, so a Document points at the named set as well as at each model. NOTHING IS REMOVED: the epoch↔RM edges and the direct Document→RM edges stay written as before, without a flag and without a mode — the group sits beside and never in between (D1, resolved by E.D. on 2026-09-10). s3Dgraphy connections datamodel including edge types with CIDOC-CRM mappings. v1.6.11 (batch ingestion, 2026-08-17): two widenings for bulk assets. has_author.source DTCProcessNode -> DTCNode, so an ACQUISITION event (D12) can carry the author of a whole lot; dtc_had_input.target += DTCNode, so a DECLARED derivation can name a whole acquisition as its input (one input, not 500 edges) — that case projects as prov:wasInformedBy, not prov:used/L10, which range over digital objects and would be wrong for an event. v1.6.8 (MIG1-A): graph-scope rights metadata become first-class nodes (DP-65). is_in_paradata_nodegroup.source += AuthorNode/LicenseNode/EmbargoNode and has_paradata_nodegroup.source += GraphNode, so the graph-self node (GraphNode) owns a graph-scope ParadataNodeGroup whose members are the AuthorNode/LicenseNode/EmbargoNode (+ the DP-65 GeoPositionNode shift), replacing the legacy graph.data['author_name'/'license'/'embargo'] fields. The Data Funnel canvas tier now reads these member nodes (one reader per scope); a one-shot load-time migration materialises the legacy fields into nodes. v1.6.7 (BUGFIX-CONN3): closes the two silent follow-ups of CONN2. has_documentation.source gains PropertyNode (judicious widening): the honest reading of a legacy yEd dashed PropertyNode→Document connector is P70i_is_documented_in ('the property is documented in this source'), NOT has_visual_reference (which CONN2 moved to PropertyNode→ResourceNode). The import heuristic (import_graphml.enhance_edge_type) now routes PropertyNode→Document to has_documentation and the rarer CombinerNode/ParadataNode→Document to generic_connection+warning (a combiner aggregates extractors and cites no document; the DTC chain is NOT synthesised at import). Shelf: hat_as_document no longer offers has_visual_reference (a Document attaches via has_documentation/extracted_from); a new hat_as_visual_resource attaches a ResourceNode image via has_visual_reference from a PropertyNode — the correct home after CONN2. No illegal edge is produced or expected. v1.6.6 (BUGFIX-CONN2): closes the two open domain questions on has_visual_reference (E.D. 2026-08-05). SOURCE narrowed to exactly [PropertyNode]: only a property (an asserted quale) is what a visual reference illustrates; the generic ParadataNode entry is dropped, which — because ExtractorNode, CombinerNode and DocumentNode are all subclasses of ParadataNode — now excludes them by class hierarchy (a PropertyNode is neither a sibling nor a parent of the others). The extractor/combiner denied_edges from v1.6.5 are therefore REDUNDANT for this edge but are KEPT as a defensive guard (they still bite if the source is ever broadened back to ParadataNode). TARGET changed from [DocumentNode] to [ResourceNode]: the oddity was that a visual reference pointed at a source-document (E31) rather than at a visual resource. It now points at the resource-layer image node (ResourceNode = E73 Information Object / ExternalResourceReference — the same P67 hinge RM/RMDoc use via has_linked_resource), keeping DocumentNode = fonte. CIDOC stays P138i_has_representation with the target co-typed E36 Visual Item: E36 is a subclass of E73, so co-typing a ResourceNode as E36 is range-consistent (it was NOT, strictly, for an E31 Document). FOLLOW-UPS flagged for E.D. (see end-of report): (a) import_graphml.enhance_edge_type still hardcodes PropertyNode/Combiner/Paradata→DocumentNode ⇒ has_visual_reference (legacy yEd heuristic, now produces an edge this datamodel refuses) — needs a domain decision on what legacy paradata→document edges become; (b) shelf.hat_as_document lists has_visual_reference among the Document-attach edges — it can no longer validate (target is ResourceNode), so a paradata attach silently no longer attaches; a hat_as_visual_resource(ResourceNode)+has_visual_reference path is the proper home. v1.6.5 (BUGFIX-CONN): has_visual_reference is no longer offered FROM an ExtractorNode or a CombinerNode. An extractor toward a document expresses ONLY extracted_from (its relation to the source is the extraction, not an illustration); a combiner aggregates extractors and illustrates nothing. Because ExtractorNode, CombinerNode and PropertyNode are all subclasses of ParadataNode, and has_visual_reference.source lists ParadataNode, simply dropping the two subtypes from the source list would not exclude them (they still match via the parent class). So this is expressed with node_type_restrictions (keyed by RUNTIME node_type, like USNt) using a new denied_edges blacklist (the mirror of allowed_edges): extractor/combiner deny has_visual_reference. PropertyNode and any other legitimate ParadataNode source keep it unchanged. OPEN domain question for E.D.: which paradata node-types may legitimately have a visual reference (today source = PropertyNode/ExtractorNode/CombinerNode/ParadataNode) — extractor/combiner removed; the rest left as-is, not invented. v1.6.1: has_paradata_nodegroup source extended to include EpochNode — an epoch can now own a ParadataNodeGroup holding its temporal-definition properties (e.g. absolute_time_start/end as PropertyNodes with paradata provenance), mirroring how a StratigraphicNode carries its paradata group. v1.6.0 (paired with node datamodel v1.6.0) introduces: bug fix on is_in_paradata_nodegroup (typo 'ProperrtyNOde' → 'PropertyNode'); semantic fix on has_documentation (P104_is_subject_to → P70i_is_documented_in — P104 means 'subject to a legal right', not 'has documentation'); deprecation of has_timebranch as duplicate of is_in_timebranch (the latter is the canonical one — used by import_graphml.py and graphml_patcher.py; the former exists only in config JSON); component list aligned with node datamodel (HDT-O, PROV-O added). HDT-O containment properties (hdto:contains_HDT, hdto:contains_SU, hdto:isPrimary) and physical-relation discriminator subproperties (em:abuts, em:cuts, em:fills, em:overlies, em:bonded_to, em:equals as rdfs:subPropertyOf crmarchaeo:AP11_has_physical_relation) to be added in v1.6.1. v1.5.3 introduced canonical/reverse directionality with verb-based labels for clear socket identification in node editors. v1.5.4 added 'has_visual_reference' edge type. v1.5.5 added 'is_in_location' edge type with context-sensitive CIDOC mapping (P53 for node→location, P89 for the recursive location→location hierarchy) and an optional 'is_primary' boolean attribute (s3d:isPrimary, proposed). v1.6.3: added node_type_restrictions — a per-node-type narrowing of the class-level edge rules (POL5): USN (the NEUTRAL stratigraphic unit, a risparmio) takes is_after/is_before and nothing else, because a void cannot cut, fill, abut or bond. v1.6.4 (POL6): the same restriction, moved to USNt — the tokens went back to their conventional meanings, USN = US negativa (all relations, it is a unit of the sequence) and USNt = US neutra (sequence only).

referenced_ontology_versions._comment: Versions of the reference ontologies this datamodel's mappings are audited against. Update via the mapping-update procedure (see docs: 'Updating the CIDOC mapping') whenever a new official release is adopted.

CRMarchaeo.note: official OWL is internally aligned to CIDOC-CRM 7.1.2 and CRMsci 2.0

node_type_restrictions._comment: PER-NODE-TYPE narrowing of what the edge_types below already allow. The edge rules are stated by CLASS, so a subtype inherits everything its parent may connect; this block is how a subtype says LESS than its parent without leaving the class hierarchy. A consumer that ignores it simply offers more, so it degrades to today's behaviour instead of breaking. Added in v1.6.3 (POL5, 2026-08-04) for the neutral stratigraphic unit.

extractor._comment: BUGFIX-CONN (v1.6.5): an ExtractorNode toward a DocumentNode expresses ONLY extracted_from. has_visual_reference (P138i, 'the paradata node is illustrated/anchored by a document') does not apply to an extraction. Because ExtractorNode is a subclass of ParadataNode and has_visual_reference.source lists ParadataNode, removing the subtype from that list would not exclude it (still matched via the parent); denied_edges is the surgical, class-hierarchy-safe way to say LESS than the parent for this ONE edge. denied_edges is the blacklist mirror of allowed_edges and is NOT scope-gated (it names exact edges to withhold).

combiner._comment: BUGFIX-CONN (v1.6.5): a CombinerNode aggregates ExtractorNodes (combines); it illustrates nothing, so it is not a source of has_visual_reference either. Same class-hierarchy reasoning as ExtractorNode.

USNt._comment: E.D.: the ONLY stratigraphic relations of the NEUTRAL unit (USNt — a risparmio: a window or door opening, a niche, the volume of a room) are is_after / is_before, and `is_before` is not an edge type of its own: it is the declared `reverse` of is_after, so naming is_after covers both readings. The reason is physical, not editorial: nothing was removed and nothing touches the void, so it cannot cut, fill, abut or bond, and sequence is the only stratigraphic statement left. NB the restriction is on USNt ALONE: the NEGATIVE unit (USN, displayed US-) is a unit of the sequence — it cuts and is filled — and keeps every relation. POL6 moved this block from USN to USNt when the two tokens went back to their conventional meanings. `scope` says which family of edges this narrows: PARADATA and membership edges (has_property, has_data_provenance, is_in_paradata_nodegroup, has_first_epoch, survive_in_epoch, is_in_activity, is_part_of, ...) are NOT restricted — a risparmio is documented, measured and dated like any other unit.

is_after.name: is_after
is_after.label: Is after
is_after.description: Indicates a temporal sequence where one item occurs after another. This is the canonical direction in Extended Matrix (from more recent to more ancient stratigraphic units).

mapping._cidoc_comment: REPAIR 2026-09-21: was crm:P120_occurs_before, which is NOT declared in CIDOC CRM 7.1.3 — the triple was inert, found by no query and used by no reasoner. crmarchaeo:AP28_occurs_before (E2 Temporal Entity -> E2 Temporal Entity, subPropertyOf P183_ends_before_the_start_of) was ALREADY this edge's extension_mapping and says exactly what was meant, so it is promoted to the primary `cidoc` term and the extension_mapping is cleared: the dual emission was sdoppiando the same fact onto one live and one dead IRI. rdf_subject:'target' is UNCHANGED and still correct — see below.
mapping._rdf_subject_comment: E.D. + measured 2026-09-20: the EM arrow runs from the MORE RECENT unit to the more ancient one, while P120/AP28 put the EARLIER entity in the subject (CIDOC: 'a temporal gap exists between the end of A and the start of B'). Emitting source-first therefore asserted the exact opposite of the stratigraphy. The projection now takes the edge TARGET as the triple subject for this mapping. Checked on Aiano: of 204 is_after edges, the 81 whose ends sit in different epochs ALL have the more recent unit as source, none the reverse.

changed_from.name: changed_from
changed_from.label: Changed from
changed_from.description: Represents an object that changes over time, indicating temporal transformation.

mapping._cidoc_comment: REPAIR 2026-09-21: was P123_resulted_from, missing the 'i' of the inverse and therefore undeclared in CIDOC CRM 7.1.3. The declared term is P123i_resulted_from (E18 Physical Thing -> E81 Transformation).

abuts.name: abuts
abuts.label: Abuts
abuts.description: This stratigraphic unit abuts against the target stratigraphic unit.

cuts.name: cuts
cuts.label: Cuts
cuts.description: This stratigraphic unit cuts the target stratigraphic unit.

fills.name: fills
fills.label: Fills
fills.description: This stratigraphic unit fills the target stratigraphic unit (e.g., a deposit filling a cut).

overlies.name: overlies
overlies.label: Overlies
overlies.description: This stratigraphic unit overlies (covers) the target stratigraphic unit.

is_bonded_to.name: is_bonded_to
is_bonded_to.label: Is bonded to
is_bonded_to.description: Older spelling of 'bonded_to' (see `spelling_of`): this stratigraphic unit is physically bonded to the target stratigraphic unit (e.g., masonry bonding). Symmetric. Accepted when read, never written: every writer emits 'bonded_to'.

bonded_to.name: bonded_to
bonded_to.label: Bonded to
bonded_to.description: Canonical (v5.0 em_data.xlsx) form of the bonding relation: this stratigraphic unit is physically bonded to the target. Symmetric. Allowed between any two StratigraphicNode instances including USVs-USVs when two virtually-reconstructed elements are theoretically bonded (e.g. two missing blocks of the same inferred course).

is_physically_equal_to.name: is_physically_equal_to
is_physically_equal_to.label: Is physically equal to
is_physically_equal_to.description: Older spelling of 'equals' (see `spelling_of`): two stratigraphic units are considered physically the same entity or continuous fabric. Symmetric. Accepted when read, never written: every writer emits 'equals'.

equals.name: equals
equals.label: Equals
equals.description: Canonical (v5.0 em_data.xlsx) form of the 'same physical entity' relation: two distinct unit IDs (from different campaigns or archival sources) refer to the same stratigraphic fact. Symmetric.

has_same_time.name: has_same_time
has_same_time.label: Has same time
has_same_time.description: Indicates that two elements are contemporaneous. This is a symmetric relation.

mapping._cidoc_comment: REPAIR 2026-09-21: was crm:P114_is_equal_in_time_to, not declared in CIDOC CRM 7.1.3. crmarchaeo:AP22_is_equal_in_time_to (E2 -> E2) was already the extension_mapping and is promoted to primary; the extension_mapping is cleared so the dual emission does not repeat one fact on a dead IRI.

has_data_provenance.name: has_data_provenance
has_data_provenance.label: Has data provenance
has_data_provenance.description: Indicates the provenance of data, often linking to source nodes.

contrasts_with.name: contrasts_with
contrasts_with.label: Contrasts with
contrasts_with.description: Represents contrasting or mutually exclusive properties. This is a symmetric relation.

mapping._cidoc_comment: CRMem 2026-09-24 (E.D.): `cidoc` LASCIATO VUOTO, ed e' una decisione. crm:P15_was_influenced_by ha dominio E7_Activity e un TimeBranch e' un E4_Period: il predicato non regge il dominio, e dice comunque un'altra cosa (influenza, non mutua esclusione). CRMinf non copre l'incompatibilita': le sue proprieta' parlano di premesse, conclusioni, adozione, provenienza e significato, e nessuna dice che due credenze si escludono, perche' modella COME si arriva a una credenza e non le relazioni logiche FRA credenze. Quindi nessuna superproprieta' onesta: l'arco esce sulla sola em:contrastsWith, come is_in_activity.

has_first_epoch.name: has_first_epoch
has_first_epoch.label: Has first epoch
has_first_epoch.description: Indicates the initial epoch associated with a node.

mapping._comment: Changed 2026-07-10: was P82a (invalid: E52->E61) + AP13 (invalid: A5->A5). Epoch attribution is an interpretive act, not a physical stratigraphic relation. em:firstAttestedInEpoch is a documented shortcut of: unit P92i was brought into existence by genesis event (SE), event P10 falls within epoch (E4). Where an SE node exists, AP25_occurs_during applies between SE and epoch. See WP3 coverage analysis Appendix B.2.

survive_in_epoch.name: survive_in_epoch
survive_in_epoch.label: Survives in epoch
survive_in_epoch.description: Indicates that a node continues to exist in a given epoch.

mapping._comment: Changed 2026-07-10: was P10 (too strong: survival through part of an epoch is overlap, not containment) + AP13 (invalid: A5->A5). The unit's spacetime volume (P196) overlaps the epoch's. See WP3 coverage analysis Appendix B.2.

survive_in_epoch._source_comment: 2026-09-21 (E.D.): FunctionalUnitNodeGroup added here AND to has_first_epoch, so a functional unit carries a temporal index of its own. The asymmetry with ActivityNodeGroup — which has has_first_epoch and deliberately does NOT have survive_in_epoch — is meant: an activity is an event and does not survive, a functional unit is a thing that persists.

has_sub_epoch.name: has_sub_epoch
has_sub_epoch.label: Has sub-epoch
has_sub_epoch.description: Splits an epoch into ordered sub-epochs (phases). Source is the parent epoch, target a phase (itself an EpochNode). Phases partition the parent's time-span; when hidden the parent epoch holds all the units, when shown the units are distributed across the phases. Reverse: is_in_epoch.

mapping._comment: EM 1.6 periodisation: epoch -> phase (sub-epoch). A phase P10 falls within its parent epoch (E4 within E4). Added 2026-07 for the EMStudio phase system.

is_in_activity.name: is_in_activity
is_in_activity.label: Is in activity
is_in_activity.description: Indicates that a node is part of a specific activity.

mapping._cidoc_comment: CRMem 2026-09-21 (E.D.): `cidoc` STAYS EMPTY and that is now a decision, not a gap. Measured against CIDOC CRM 7.1.3 and CRMarchaeo 2.1.1, no generic CRM predicate holds: P9i_forms_part_of needs an E4 Period in the SUBJECT and none of the sources here is one; P129i_is_subject_of needs an E89 in the OBJECT and ActivityNodeGroup is E7 Activity, whose ancestors are E5/E4/E2/E1/E92; P12i_was_present_at would pass the type check (E28 reaches E77 via E71/E70) but would be false, because a PropertyNode attended nothing. CRMarchaeo has no generic activity class and none of its 32 AP properties expresses membership in one. So the connector lives in CRMem as em:isInActivity (domain E1, range E7_Activity, NO superproperty), declared in em.ttl. The CLASS is not ours: E7_Activity is CIDOC core and stays the mapping of ActivityNodeGroup — only the property is new. Renamed from the dead desideratum CIDOC-S3D:participatedInActivity, which claimed a participation this model does not assert. _serialize_edge now emits a declared-absent edge on its extension predicate alone rather than staying silent: the silence was correct only while there was nothing true to say. PREVIOUS NOTE (repair pass, kept for the record): REPAIR 2026-09-21 (verso): LEFT DELIBERATELY EMPTY — DECISIONE PER E.D. Was P9_consists_of (E4 Period -> E4 Period), emitted source-first, so the triple read 'this stratigraphic unit consists of that activity': reversed AND domain-violating. Neither candidate holds, measured against CIDOC CRM 7.1.3: (a) P9i_forms_part_of needs an E4 Period in the SUBJECT, and the sources here are StratigraphicNode / PropertyNode / DocumentNode / ExtractorNode / CombinerNode / ParadataNode(Group) — none is an E4; (b) P129i_is_subject_of needs an E89 Propositional Object in the OBJECT, and ActivityNodeGroup is E7 Activity, whose ancestors are E5/E4/E2/E1/E92 — not E89. Nothing was invented in the gap. CONSEQUENCE to weigh: with `cidoc` empty the exporter's fallback writes crm:P130_shows_features_of (see _serialize_edge), which is a live IRI stating something else again, and the CIDOC-S3D extension_mapping below is not emitted at all on that branch.

is_in_location.name: is_in_location
is_in_location.label: Is in location
is_in_location.description: Indicates that a node belongs to a spatial / locational group (LocationNodeGroup). Membership is m:n (multiple is_in_location edges per source are allowed) and additive (memberships compose; none overrides). The optional 'is_primary' attribute on at most one edge per source disambiguates which membership is rendered as a yEd group folder in em-graph. The same edge type also carries the recursive Location → Location hierarchy (Pompei → Sector 4 → Casa del Fauno → Room 12).

node_to_location.applies_when: source is StratigraphicNode | ParadataNode | ParadataNodeGroup | DocumentNode | ExtractorNode | CombinerNode | PropertyNode and target is LocationNodeGroup
node_to_location.rationale: CIDOC-core P53 is the canonical predicate connecting an entity to an E53 Place. No s3d: extension predicate is needed.

location_to_location.applies_when: source is LocationNodeGroup and target is LocationNodeGroup (recursive hierarchy)
location_to_location.rationale: CIDOC-core P89 expresses Place-within-Place; reused as-is for the recursive containment of LocationNodeGroups. No s3d: extension predicate is needed.

is_primary.description: If true, this membership is the primary one for the source node and is rendered as a yEd group folder in em-graph. At most one is_primary=true edge per source node. Additional memberships render as labels/badges on the node (yEd cannot draw overlapping group folders).

mapping.rationale: No CIDOC-core or CRMarchaeo equivalent — is_primary is a UX/rendering disambiguation flag for the m:n membership pattern (specifically: which membership becomes the yEd group folder in em-graph). Carrying it in the s3d extension namespace preserves the information through a SPARQL round-trip from a CIDOC triplestore. Candidate primitive for a forthcoming CIDOC-S3D extension.

has_property.name: has_property
has_property.label: Has property
has_property.description: Connects a node to one of its properties.

mapping._comment: Changed 2026-07-10: AP9_took_matter_from removed (invalid: A4 Stratigraphic Genesis -> S10 Material Substantial, unrelated to property attribution). em:hasQualia is the EM-native predicate declared in em.ttl. See WP3 coverage analysis section 10. SOURCE WIDENED 2026-08-11 (v1.6.10) to RepresentationModelDocNode: an RMDoc is the SPATIALISATION of a document (the historical photograph put back where it was taken from, with its camera), and a spatialisation is a reconstruction — therefore a claim, and a claim must be able to say how it is known. Giving the RMDoc its own properties is what lets it declare the pose and, through the ordinary paradata chain, where the pose came from (a measurement, a feature matching, a known point). Only the STRUCTURAL permission is granted here: the mathematics of camera and pose belongs to the tool that computes it, not to the datamodel.

extracted_from.name: extracted_from
extracted_from.label: Extracted from
extracted_from.description: Indicates that information is derived from a particular source: a source DOCUMENT, or (since v1.6.10) an ANNOTATION REGION — the traced part of an image that a reading is based on.

mapping._comment: TARGET WIDENED 2026-08-11 (v1.6.10) to AnnotationRegionNode, NOT a new edge type, and the choice is worth the paragraph. The relation 'this extraction is based on that' already exists and already has a name; a dedicated `derived_from_region` would be a SECOND name for one relation, and a reader following a provenance chain would have to know both to follow it. The CRMinf mapping is what makes the widening honest rather than convenient: J7_is_based_on_evidence_from takes EVIDENCE, and a traced region is evidence — a more precise citation than the whole picture, in the same way a page number is more precise than a book. The region stays reachable to its own source through is_on_resource, so the chain extractor → region → image loses nothing. NOTE the asymmetry with ResourceNode, which is deliberately NOT a target: a file is not something one can cite, which is why annotating a bare resource MINTS a Document beside it (see annotation/paradata.py::_source_document) instead of widening this edge further.

combines.name: combines
combines.label: Combines
combines.description: Indicates that a node combines information from various sources.

is_in_timebranch.name: is_in_timebranch
is_in_timebranch.label: Is in timebranch
is_in_timebranch.description: Indicates that a node belongs to a specific time branch.

has_timebranch.name: has_timebranch
has_timebranch.label: Has timebranch
has_timebranch.deprecated_reason: Duplicate of is_in_timebranch with identical mapping and allowed_connections. Verified usage in /src: is_in_timebranch is the canonical form (used by importer/import_graphml.py:1510 and exporter/graphml/graphml_patcher.py:73); has_timebranch exists only in JSON config files (this one + em_visual_rules.json). Kept temporarily for backward compatibility on read; writers MUST emit is_in_timebranch. Scheduled for removal in 1.7.0.
has_timebranch.description: [DEPRECATED in 1.6.0 — use is_in_timebranch] Indicates that a node is connected to a specific time branch.

validated_by.name: validated_by
validated_by.label: Validated by
validated_by.description: A HUMAN author endorses a piece of content: they have read it and put their name to it. Introduced for EM Narrative (N4) to carry the act at the heart of 'Who Made This?': a machine may draft, but only a person can vouch. Until this edge exists, AI-authored content is a draft and says so — the absence of the edge IS the unendorsed state, so nothing can claim endorsement it has not received.
validated_by.scope_note: Distinct from has_author, and the distinction is the point. has_author says who WROTE it (human or AI, prov:wasAttributedTo). validated_by says who ACCEPTED RESPONSIBILITY for it, and the target is deliberately AuthorNode only — never AuthorAINode: a model endorsing a model would be a signature with nobody behind it. It is also NOT a quality judgement or a peer review: it records that a named person stands behind this content, nothing more and nothing less.

mapping._comment: NEEDS AN ONTOLOGY DECISION (E.D.). Endorsement has no exact term in CIDOC-CRM or PROV-O: crm:P14_carried_out_by would require reifying an E7 Activity we do not author, and crminf's belief machinery (I2/J4) models what someone holds TRUE, not what they take responsibility for. prov:wasInfluencedBy is used as the domain-neutral anchor because it is true (the content was influenced by the validator's act) and claims nothing more; the precise meaning lives in the em: extension. If a validation ACT is later reified as an E13 Attribute Assignment, this mapping is where it changes.

has_author.name: has_author
has_author.label: Has author
has_author.description: Represents the connection of a node with its author. Target can be an AuthorNode (human) or AuthorAINode (AI-assisted authoring). Source covers the full range of EM node types so that the resolver can walk from any scope level down to the author. SOURCE WIDENED 2026-08-16 (asset DTC protocol): ResourceNode joins the list. 'Who took this photograph' is exactly prov:wasAttributedTo on an information object, and the mapping is already domain-neutral — the omission was an oversight of scope, not a semantic boundary: the list exists so the resolver can walk from ANY scope down to the author, and a resource is a scope somebody attributes. It is also the shape the asset enrichment protocol needs, where the AUTHOR of the bytes (possibly absent, possibly dead) is declared by an ATTRIBUTOR who is somebody else (s3dgraphy.rights.enrich_asset_dtc, docs/asset-dtc-protocol.md).

mapping._comment: Changed 2026-07-10: was P94_has_created (invalid: domain E65 Creation, range E28 Conceptual Object - cannot hold for physical SU nodes) + L10_had_input (describes digital machine events, not authorship). prov:wasAttributedTo is domain-neutral (any entity -> agent) and covers human and AI authors uniformly; PROV-O is already a declared component. Property-graph JSON untouched: importers and Heriverse unaffected. See WP3 coverage analysis section 10.

allowed_connections._note: SOURCE WIDENED 2026-08-17 (batch ingestion): DTCProcessNode -> DTCNode, the DTC event BASE class, so an ACQUISITION (DTCAcquisitionNode, D12) can carry an author too — the same fix already applied to dtc_had_input/dtc_had_output for the same reason. A campaign of four hundred photographs is attributed ONCE, on the event that brought them in, and the reader (s3dgraphy.rights) already walks the chain to find it; without this the batch attribution silently degraded to generic_connection and the licence became unreadable.

has_geoposition.name: has_geoposition
has_geoposition.label: Has geoposition
has_geoposition.description: Represents a connection with the geoposition node of a given node.

mapping._cidoc_comment: REPAIR 2026-09-21: the crmgeo:Q4_has_spatial_projection extension_mapping is REMOVED (E.D.). crm:P53_has_former_or_current_location (E18 Physical Thing -> E53 Place) is valid and sufficient on its own; no extension is needed here. MEASURED, and worth knowing before anyone puts it back: Q4 IS declared, both in CRMgeo 1.2 (FORTH namespace) and in the CRMgeo 2.0 draft served at the http://www.cidoc-crm.org/extensions/crmgeo/ namespace this datamodel emits. The removal is a modelling decision, not a dead-IRI repair.

has_linked_resource.name: has_linked_resource
has_linked_resource.label: Has linked resource
has_linked_resource.description: Connects a node to its linked resource(s).

has_representation_model.name: has_representation_model
has_representation_model.label: Has representation model
has_representation_model.description: Connects epochs with their representation models in 3D space.

allowed_connections._note: EM16-RMNG widens the TARGET with RepresentationModelNodeGroup so a Document can point at a named set as well as at each model. The direct Document→model edges are NOT replaced: D1 of the 2026-09-10 spec was resolved by E.D. as additive-pure, and 1.6 already relies on this edge carrying the Document→RM bond (commit c46b365, where epoch-edge cleanup picks by epoch endpoint and not by edge type precisely so the Document bond survives).

has_representation_model_doc.name: has_representation_model_doc
has_representation_model_doc.label: Has document representation model
has_representation_model_doc.description: Connects extractors, combiners and documents node to their representation model in 3D space.

has_representation_model_sf.name: has_representation_model_sf
has_representation_model_sf.label: Has special find representation model
has_representation_model_sf.description: Connects special find units to their representation model in 3D space.

reverse.name: is_sf_representation_model_of
reverse.label: Is special find representation model of

has_semantic_shape.name: has_semantic_shape
has_semantic_shape.label: Has semantic shape
has_semantic_shape.description: Connects any node to its semantic shape representation in 3D space. Since v1.6.10 this is ALSO how a PropertyNode of type 'geometry' carries its payload: the proxy of a unit is a property, and the numbers (convex hulls / spheres, or a .glb via the shape's url) live in the SemanticShapeNode it points at. The source stays 'Node' — deliberately, and now for a reason worth writing down: narrowing it to the stratigraphic types would break the proxy-as-property model, which needs a PropertyNode to be a legal source.

mapping._comment: PROXY-AS-PROPERTY (2026-08-11, v1.6.10): a PropertyNode(property_type='geometry') → SemanticShapeNode is the payload link of the proxy. No change was needed to the allowed_connections (source was already 'Node', which a PropertyNode satisfies) — this comment exists so the permissiveness is not 'tidied up' later by someone who does not know it is load-bearing. Semantics unchanged: the shape is a representation of whatever points at it; what changed is WHO points at it (the property, not the unit directly) and therefore that the geometry now has a paradata chain.

is_in_paradata_nodegroup.name: is_in_paradata_nodegroup
is_in_paradata_nodegroup.label: Is in paradata nodegroup
is_in_paradata_nodegroup.description: Indicates that a node is included into a paradata node group. Standard members are the paradata-chain nodes (PropertyNode/DocumentNode/ExtractorNode/CombinerNode/ParadataNode); GeoPositionNode is additionally admitted so the per-graph georeferencing shift can be a member of the graph-scope ParadataNodeGroup (DP-65) — semantically valid only at graph scope. v1.6.8 (MIG1-A): source widened further with AuthorNode/LicenseNode/EmbargoNode so the graph-scope rights metadata (author/license/embargo) live as first-class member nodes of the graph-scope ParadataNodeGroup (DP-65), replacing the legacy graph.data['author_name'/'license'/'embargo'] fields — again meaningful at graph scope (anchored on the GraphNode via has_paradata_nodegroup).

mapping._cidoc_comment: REPAIR 2026-09-21 (verso): was P106_is_composed_of, emitted source-first with no rdf_subject:'target', so the triple read 'this property is composed of that paradata group' — the membership stated backwards. P106i_forms_part_of (E90 Symbolic Object -> E90 Symbolic Object) is the declared inverse and is preferred to rdf_subject because it is one indirection less. Range holds: ParadataNodeGroup is an E90 through em:NodeGroup (E73 Information Object).

has_paradata_nodegroup.name: has_paradata_nodegroup
has_paradata_nodegroup.label: Has paradata nodegroup
has_paradata_nodegroup.description: Indicates that a node belongs to a paradata node group. v1.6.8 (MIG1-A): source widened with GraphNode so the graph itself (GraphNode = the graph-self node) can own the graph-scope ParadataNodeGroup (DP-65) that holds the author/license/embargo member nodes — mirroring how a StratigraphicNode or an EpochNode carries its own paradata group.

mapping._cidoc_comment: REPAIR 2026-09-21 (verso): was P70_documents, emitted source-first, which made the stratigraphic unit an E31 Document documenting its own paradata group — domain violated AND the proposition reversed. P129i_is_subject_of (E1 CRM Entity -> E89 Propositional Object) says the right thing in the right direction: the unit is the subject of the body of reasoning gathered about it. Its range is why ParadataNodeGroup moves to E89 Propositional Object in the node datamodel the same day.

has_license.name: has_license
has_license.label: Has license
has_license.description: Indicates that a resource is subject to a specific license.

has_embargo.name: has_embargo
has_embargo.label: Has embargo
has_embargo.description: Indicates that an element is subject to a temporal embargo. Source can be any node (GraphNode for canvas-wide embargo, LicenseNode for license-scoped embargo, or any node for node-scoped embargo), mirroring has_license.

has_documentation.name: has_documentation
has_documentation.label: Has documentation
has_documentation.description: Indicates that the element has an associated documentation node.

mapping.rationale: P70i_is_documented_in (inverse of P70_documents) is the canonical CRM predicate to link an entity to a document about it. Earlier v1.5.5 used P104_is_subject_to which is semantically wrong (P104 means 'subject to a legal right or rule', not 'has documentation about it'). v1.6.7 (BUGFIX-CONN3): PropertyNode added to source — a property (an asserted quale) may be documented in a source-document (P70i reads true). This is the honest reading of a legacy yEd dashed connector PropertyNode→Document, now that has_visual_reference (CONN2) points at a ResourceNode image and no longer at a Document. Widening is deliberately limited to PropertyNode: a CombinerNode aggregates extractors and a bare ParadataNode carry no documentation relation, so those legacy endpoints are left as generic_connection with a warning at import rather than asserting P70i (the DTC evidence chain property<-combiner<-extractor->document is NOT synthesised at import).

has_visual_reference.name: has_visual_reference
has_visual_reference.label: Has visual reference
has_visual_reference.description: Indicates that the element has an associated visual reference.

mapping._comment: Mapped 2026-07-10; source/target revised 2026-08-05 (BUGFIX-CONN2). A PropertyNode (an asserted quale) is visually illustrated/anchored by a VISUAL RESOURCE — the resource-layer image node (ResourceNode), NOT a source-document. E36 Visual Item P138 represents E1; edge direction property->resource matches P138i, consistent with the has_representation_model family. The exporter co-types the target (the ResourceNode) as E36 Visual Item; because E36 is a subclass of E73 Information Object (the ResourceNode's base class) this co-typing is range-consistent — it was strained for the former E31 Document target. Distinct from has_linked_resource (P67, a bare resource reference) and from extracted_from (P67/J7, an extraction source): a visual reference SHOWS a property, an extraction source JUSTIFIES an inference. DocumentNode stays a source (fonte). See WP3 coverage analysis Appendix B.1 and the CIDOC note for Felicetti in the end-of report. TARGET WIDENED 2026-08-11 (2D annotator, v1.6.9): AnnotationRegionNode joins ResourceNode, because the most precise visual reference is the REGION, not the whole picture — 'this quale is shown HERE in this photograph'. The region is already an E36 Visual Item in its own right, so P138i needs no co-typing for it: the range fits without being widened. Pointing at the whole image stays legal and stays the right thing to say when the region is not known.

is_on_resource.name: is_on_resource
is_on_resource.label: Is on resource
is_on_resource.description: An AnnotationRegion is a region OF a specific image (or of one page of a multi-page resource): this edge says which. Region -> ResourceNode/DocumentNode. The region also keeps the id in its own data.resource_id, so it is readable alone; this edge is the graph's statement of it.

mapping._comment: Added 2026-08-11 (2D annotator, semantics first). A NEW edge type rather than a reuse of is_part_of, for two reasons that both matter. (1) SEMANTICS: is_part_of maps to P46i_forms_part_of, PHYSICAL containment between things — a special find inside a wall. A region is not physically inside a photograph; it is an informational part of a symbolic object, which is P106i (E90 Symbolic Object P106 is composed of E90). (2) DRAWING: is_part_of is the NESTING axis of the EM drawing (one primary parent, rendered as a box around its members, invariant 5), so reusing it would make every region a member box inside its image in the matrix — a layout claim nobody made. Distinct from has_linked_resource (P67, a bare reference from anything to a resource): this one says the source IS part of the target.

is_part_of.name: is_part_of
is_part_of.label: Is part of
is_part_of.description: Mereological (part–whole) PHYSICAL containment, not chronological or stratigraphic: a Special Find reused inside a wall, tile fragments inside a reconstructed roof (DP-36). Containment is a relationship, not a change in node type: a US that contains elements is still a US, and the presence of is_part_of edges is the only discriminant that identifies it as a container. This is the NESTING axis — one primary parent, drawn as a box around its members — so a FunctionalUnitNodeGroup is NOT a target here (its membership is the m:n tag axis is_in_functional_unit, DP-72). A Functional Unit may however be a SOURCE: a whole component physically embedded in a stratigraphic unit (a column engaged in a later wall).

extension_when._comment: AP21i ranges STRICTLY over A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit, and in this datamodel only StratigraphicUnit (US) maps to A2: DocumentaryStratigraphicUnit and the virtual units map to A8 Stratigraphic Unit, VirtualSpecialFindUnit to E89/E19, FunctionalUnitNodeGroup to E24. Emitting AP21i at those targets would be range-inconsistent, so the extension predicate is emitted only when the container is a US. The core P46i goes out for every containment regardless. FORWARD NOTE (2026-09-25, E.D.): this condition is tied to A2, not to the US as such. CRMba 1.4 declares B5 Stratigraphic Building Unit a SUBCLASS OF A2 — the very term the built-heritage gap points at, the one that would stop masonry and revetment units flattening onto the soil-unit type — so the day that subtyping is adopted, whatever node class carries B5 must be added here or the refinement switches itself off on exactly the masonry case. CRMba is NOT adopted today and is deliberately absent from referenced_ontology_versions: version 1.4 is a draft of April 2016, five classes, and it aligns itself to CRMarchaeo 2.0 and CRMsci 2.0, both earlier than the releases this datamodel is audited against.

mapping.rationale: P46i_forms_part_of is the correct GENERIC projection and stays: containment in EM is mereological. It is however weaker than what CRMarchaeo offers for the archaeologically central case — an object found inside a stratigraphic unit. AP21 contains / AP21i is contained in is the CRMarchaeo shortcut for the full path E18 -AP18i- A7 Embedding -AP19- A2, and A7 Embedding's scope note covers exactly the distinction that matters here: an embedding is normally stable from the generation of the A2 that surrounds it, but 'may also be due to later intrusion'. Emitting AP21i beside P46i is a REFINEMENT, not a correction: AP18 is declared rdfs:subPropertyOf P46_is_composed_of in CRMarchaeo v2.1.1, so readers of P46 keep seeing what they saw and no existing export is invalidated. REPAIR 2026-09-25: the slot previously held P46_is_composed_of, the INVERSE of the core predicate. The exporter emits the extension with the same subject and object as the core, so every containment was also asserting that the part is composed of the whole. Same fault found and fixed in is_in_functional_unit and is_in_representation_model_group.

allowed_connections._note: ReusedSpecialFind added 2026-09-25: the manual states 'the host SU acts as container for the RSF' and this edge's own description cites 'a Special Find reused inside a wall', but RSF was missing from the source list, so spolia could not be attached to its host masonry. It was already allowed in is_in_functional_unit, which is what showed the omission to be an oversight and not a rule.

is_in_functional_unit.name: is_in_functional_unit
is_in_functional_unit.label: Is in functional unit
is_in_functional_unit.description: Membership of a stratigraphic unit in a FunctionalUnitNodeGroup (DP-72): the units that together make up one recognisable architectural component — the column made of its US. A Functional Unit may itself be a member of another one (the capital inside the column). This is a TAG axis, not a nesting axis: membership is m:n and additive, it does NOT claim the member's primary drawing parent, and it does not constrain the member's epoch. That distinction is the whole reason this edge exists alongside is_part_of, which projects to the same CIDOC property: a Functional Unit legitimately spans epochs (a wall built across four of them still carries the roof as one body), and a swimlane box cannot — so the functional reading lives in its own view, beside pure stratigraphy, without either constraining the other. Orthogonal to is_in_activity (intention), is_in_location (place) and the epoch axis (time).

mapping.rationale: The relation IS mereological — the component is composed of its units — so it projects exactly like is_part_of (P46i / P46). The two edges are distinct in the EM language, not in RDF: is_part_of is the nesting axis (single primary parent, drawn as a containing box, propagates lane assignment), is_in_functional_unit is a tag axis that every view opts into. Consumers that only read the RDF projection see one uniform part-whole relation, which is correct. extension_mapping cleared 2026-09-25: it held P46_is_composed_of, the inverse of the core predicate, emitted in the same direction (see is_part_of). No CRMarchaeo refinement applies here: the target is a FunctionalUnitNodeGroup (E24 Physical Human-Made Thing), not an A2 Stratigraphic Volume Unit, so AP21i does not hold. P46i alone is the correct and complete projection.

allowed_connections._note: The concrete stratigraphic classes are listed one by one, mirroring is_part_of, instead of the base 'StratigraphicNode'. That base name is NOT usable here: Node.node_type_map is keyed by node_type, and 'StratigraphicNode' happens to be the node_type of VirtualStratigraphicUnit, so Graph.validate_connection would resolve it to that single subclass and refuse every other unit. VirtualStratigraphicUnit covers USVs/USVn by subclassing.

has_digital_twin.name: has_digital_twin
has_digital_twin.label: Has digital twin
has_digital_twin.description: Links a real-world heritage entity (or any node representing one) to its Heritage Digital Twin (HDTNode). HDT-O HP1 per ECHOES D7.1 §4.2.

mapping.rationale: Per D7.1 §4.2 HP1: 'links a CH entity with a corresponding digital twin that aggregates structured knowledge about it'. Quantification many-to-many (0,n : 0,n).

has_digital_twin_component.name: has_digital_twin_component
has_digital_twin_component.label: Has digital twin component
has_digital_twin_component.description: Hierarchical containment between HDTs. A parent HDT has component child-HDTs. HDT-O HP3 (inverse) per ECHOES D7.1 §4.2. Use case: Colosseo_HDT_overall has_digital_twin_component Colosseo_HDT_Flavian / Colosseo_HDT_medieval_fortress / Colosseo_HDT_christian_site_1800. Transitive: chains of containment are inferred.

mapping.rationale: Per D7.1 §4.2 HP3: 'enables the hierarchical organization of digital twins, allowing the digital twin of a specific asset to be part of a larger digital twin representing a city, archaeological site, or cultural landscape'. Component is not limited to physical/geographical: encompasses any main-associated relationship. Quantification many-to-many (0,n : 0,n).

contains_proposition_set.name: contains_proposition_set
contains_proposition_set.label: Contains proposition set
contains_proposition_set.description: Links an HDT (HDTNode) to a Heritage Proposition Set (GraphNode / em:EMGraph) it currently aggregates. HDT-O HP33 per ECHOES D7.1 §4.2. This is the canonical way to attach an EM graph to an HDT. An EM graph can be a proposition set of multiple HDTs (many-to-many).

mapping.rationale: Per D7.1 §4.2 HP33: 'associates an HC2 HDT with an HC16 Heritage Proposition Set currently valid within it'. Version chains tracked via HP30 added / HP31 deleted / HP32 replaced. Deprecation tracked via HP34 contained (was proposition set of).

has_digital_object_part.name: has_digital_object_part
has_digital_object_part.label: Has digital object part
has_digital_object_part.description: Links an HDT (or any HC14 Volatile Digital Object) to an auxiliary digital object that is NOT a proposition set — e.g., a 3D survey database, a point cloud, a generic linked resource. HDT-O HP29 per ECHOES D7.1 §4.2.

mapping.rationale: Per D7.1 §4.2 HP29: 'associates an HC14 Volatile Digital Object with a structural part that is itself a digital object'. Subproperty of crm:P106_is_composed_of. Example: HDT of Pisa Leaning Tower has digital part a 3D survey project database (crmdig:D1).

includes_study.name: includes_study
includes_study.label: Includes study
includes_study.description: Links an HC13 Project to an HC9 Study carried out within it. D7.1 defines no direct HC13->HC9 property; modelled with CIDOC-CRM crm:P9_consists_of (activity/period composition) via the extension mechanism — consistent with HDT-O HP20 'was carried out under' being a subproperty of crm:P9i.

mapping.rationale: No HDT-O property connects HC13 Project to HC9 Study directly (D7.1). Both are activities (E7 subset of E4 Period), so crm:P9_consists_of expresses 'Project includes Study'. Aligns with HP20, itself a crm:P9i subproperty.

study_about_heritage.name: study_about_heritage
study_about_heritage.label: Study is about heritage entity
study_about_heritage.description: Links an HC9 Study to the HC1 Heritage Entity it investigated. HDT-O HP23 per ECHOES D7.1.

mapping.rationale: Per D7.1 HP23 'was about (was subject of)': Domain HC9 Study, Range HC1 Heritage Entity. Subproperty of crm:E7.P16 used specific object. Quantification many-to-many, necessary.

study_produced_proposition_set.name: study_produced_proposition_set
study_produced_proposition_set.label: Study produced proposition set
study_produced_proposition_set.description: Links an HC9 Study to the documentary output it created — in EM the proposition set (HC16 / em:EMGraph / GraphNode). HDT-O HP25 per ECHOES D7.1.

mapping.rationale: Per D7.1 HP25 'has created (was created by)': Domain HC9 Study, Range crm:E31 Document (subproperty of crm:E65.P94). The EM proposition set (HC16/em:EMGraph, an E73 Information Object) is the study's created documentary output; range widened E31->E73/HC16 and documented here.

heritage_part_of.name: heritage_part_of
heritage_part_of.label: Is part of heritage entity
heritage_part_of.description: Part-whole BETWEEN Heritage Entities (HC1): the source entity forms part of the target entity — e.g. the porphyry Tetrarchs (HC1) forms part of San Marco (HC1). D7.1 declares no HC1->HC1 part-whole property; modelled with CIDOC-CRM crm:P46i_forms_part_of via the extension mechanism.

mapping.rationale: No HDT-O property connects HC1 Heritage Entity to HC1 Heritage Entity (D7.1). crm:P46 is composed of / P46i forms part of expresses part-whole; source = part, target = whole (reverse heritage_has_part = crm:P46_is_composed_of). Domain/range E18 Physical Thing => fits tangible heritage (HC3 aspect of HC1); intangible-entity composition is deferred.

dtc_had_input.name: dtc_had_input
dtc_had_input.label: DTC process had input
dtc_had_input.description: DTC chain: a processing step (DTCProcess) consumed an input RESOURCE — a raw acquisition (photo/laser scan/…) = the ResourceNode (E73/D1). ECHOES DTC substrate profile. Dual projection CRMdig + PROV-O.

mapping.rationale: crmdig:L10_had_input (D7 Digital Machine Event -> input digital object). Dual-emitted with prov:used (Activity used Entity) — same direction (Process -> input Resource) — so CRMdig and PROV-O readers both see the acquisition consumption. Target is the Resource (ResourceNode); the input is a resource, symmetric to the output. TARGET WIDENED 2026-08-17: when the target is a DTC EVENT (an acquisition consumed as a whole lot) neither L10_had_input nor prov:used holds — both range over digital OBJECTS, and an event is not one. That case projects as prov:wasInformedBy (activity -> activity), applied in the RDF exporter (_serialize_edge); the property-graph edge stays the one edge type, because 'this output came from that input' is one sentence whether the input is a file or a campaign.

allowed_connections._note: Source is the DTC event BASE class: both step types link to their Resources — DTCProcessNode (genesis, D7) and DTCAcquisitionNode (acquisition/ingestion, D12), per the dtc_nodes section note. Listing only DTCProcessNode used to pass by accident, because the old validator could not resolve the name and fell back to accepting anything. TARGET 2026-08-17: DTCNode joins ResourceNode so a DECLARED derivation can name a whole ACQUISITION as its input — the serial node exists precisely so a campaign of 500 photographs is one input and not 500 edges. The RDF projection distinguishes the two cases (see mapping.rationale); dtc_derived_from stays resource -> resource, because a shortcut between files cannot be written to an event, and that is reported rather than faked.

dtc_had_output.name: dtc_had_output
dtc_had_output.label: DTC process had output
dtc_had_output.description: DTC chain: a processing step (DTCProcess) produced a RESOURCE (a file: mesh/orthophoto/table…) — the ResourceNode (E73/D1), which is the SHARED HINGE that a RepresentationModel and/or a Document may reference. The produced ResourceNode carries data.dtc_kind + resource_type. ECHOES DTC substrate profile. Dual projection CRMdig + PROV-O.

mapping.rationale: crmdig:L11_had_output (D7 Digital Machine Event -> produced digital object). Dual-emitted with prov:generated (Activity generated Entity) — same direction (Process -> Output). Target is the Resource (ResourceNode) — the output is a resource, not a RepresentationModel/Document (those merely reference it).

allowed_connections._note: Source is the DTC event BASE class: both step types link to their Resources — DTCProcessNode (genesis, D7) and DTCAcquisitionNode (acquisition/ingestion, D12), per the dtc_nodes section note. Listing only DTCProcessNode used to pass by accident, because the old validator could not resolve the name and fell back to accepting anything.

dtc_happened_on_device.name: dtc_happened_on_device
dtc_happened_on_device.label: Happened on device
dtc_happened_on_device.description: The APPARATUS a DTC step happened on — the camera, the scanner, the drone, the workstation. CONTEXT, NOT CHAIN: it deliberately carries no `dtc_role`, so a provenance walk does not traverse it (see _dtc_role_note: an edge without dtc_role is context by construction). A device is not a ring of the chain: it has no inputs and no outputs, and a walk that entered one would leave the flow to describe a thing.

mapping.rationale: crmdig:L12_happened_on_device (D7 Digital Machine Event -> D8 Digital Device) says exactly this and nothing else, and CRMdig keeps it separate from L10_had_input ON PURPOSE: the photographs are the input, the camera is not. Flatten the two and «which files did this body take» stops being askable, which is the only reason this edge was added. NO PROV-O PROJECTION, and that is a decision rather than an omission. prov:used is already how dtc_had_input projects, and reusing it here would collapse in PROV exactly the distinction CRMdig draws; prov:wasAssociatedWith ranges over prov:Agent, 'a thing that bears some form of responsibility for an activity', and a camera bears none. PROV-O has no device, so this edge does not project into it — the same honesty dtc_had_input applies when it says L10/prov:used do NOT hold for an acquisition as input and projects prov:wasInformedBy instead. A reader that only speaks PROV sees the step and its files, and does not see a false statement about an agent.

allowed_connections._note: SOURCE is the DTC event BASE class, like dtc_had_input: both step types run on an apparatus — DTCProcessNode (a reconstruction ran on a workstation) and DTCAcquisitionNode (a campaign ran on a camera). TARGET is DTCDeviceNode only: the device is a thing in the world and not a step, which is why it is NOT a DTCNode subclass — making it one would have put it in the chain by inheritance and set the class hierarchy arguing with dtc_role. A RIG is drawn as two devices, not as a device pointing at another: 'the sensor was on the drone' is a statement about the assembly and it has no edge here yet — see HW1's end-of, where it is named and deliberately not invented.

dtc_derived_from.name: dtc_derived_from
dtc_derived_from.label: DTC output derived from input
dtc_derived_from.description: DTC chain: the produced RESOURCE (ResourceNode) was derived from an acquisition (DTCInput) — the direct provenance shortcut alongside the process. ECHOES DTC substrate profile. Dual projection CRMdig + PROV-O.

mapping.rationale: crmdig:L21_used_as_derivation_source (derived object -> source object) with prov:wasDerivedFrom (Entity derived from Entity) — same direction (output Resource -> Input). Expresses derivation directly, independent of naming the process.

has_registration_transform.name: has_registration_transform
has_registration_transform.label: Placed by
has_registration_transform.description: A produced RESOURCE (a reconstructed model) is placed in space by a RegistrationTransform — the 7-parameter similarity solved for it. The absence of this edge is a statement too: a model nobody placed. Re-registration adds a NEW transform node and a new edge; the superseded one stays, because moving a model is provenance, not an edit.

mapping.rationale: The transform is an information object ABOUT the model, so the CRM property runs transform -P67_refers_to-> model. The EM-native edge reads from the model (the direction every consumer traverses: 'where do I put this file?'), so the projection is the inverse P67i. No PROV-O dual: PROV has nothing to say about spatial placement, and inventing one would be noise.

allowed_connections._note: Source is the ResourceNode (E73/D1), the shared hinge a RepresentationModel or a Document may reference — the same target the DTC output edge uses, so the model that was produced and the model that was placed are one node.

has_gcp_set.name: has_gcp_set
has_gcp_set.label: Solved from control points
has_gcp_set.description: A RegistrationTransform was solved from a GCPSet — the evidence behind the placement. Present ONLY in absolute mode: a transform with no such edge is a site-local frame, and the missing edge is what tells a reader so without having to trust a flag.

mapping.rationale: The same argument dtc_derived_from already makes, applied one layer up: CRM routes derivation through the event, and the event (crmdig:D7) IS in the graph — this edge is the direct shortcut between the derived object (the transform) and its source (the control set), in the same direction, so it can be read without naming the process.

generic_connection.name: generic_connection
generic_connection.label: Generic connection
generic_connection.description: Represents a non-specific connection between two nodes. This is a symmetric relation.

is_in_representation_model_group.name: is_in_representation_model_group
is_in_representation_model_group.label: Is in representation model group
is_in_representation_model_group.description: Membership of a representation model in a RepresentationModelNodeGroup (EM16-RMNG): the models that together form one named set published under a single Document — «Survey 2015» under D.01, «Reconstruction» under D.09. THE GROUP SITS BESIDE, IT DOES NOT REPLACE: every member keeps its own epoch edges (has_first_epoch / survive_in_epoch) and the Document keeps its DIRECT has_representation_model edges to each model. This edge is added on top and never put in between, so a consumer that ignores it reads exactly what it read before. Membership is a TAG axis like is_in_functional_unit and is_in_location — the member carries the edge and the group claims nothing of it — with one difference that is semantic: membership here is 1:1, not m:n. A mesh belongs to exactly one container, which is the rule already in force on the Blender side (EM-blender-tools rm_manager/containers.py, where mesh_names is authoritative). A group may legally be EMPTY and may legally have no Document: both are states the RM Manager UI already shows, and neither is validated away.

mapping.rationale: Mereological, exactly like is_in_functional_unit (DP-72): the named set IS composed of its models, so it projects as P46i / P46. The precedent is deliberate — that edge already established that a typed aggregation's membership projects to the same CIDOC property as is_part_of while staying a distinct edge in the EM language, and that consumers reading only the RDF projection correctly see one uniform part-whole relation. NOTE, AND IT IS NOT AN OVERSIGHT: this says nothing about where `digital representation of` grafts into the ontological mapping (P138i / CIDOC-S3D:has3DRepresentation and its CRMdig neighbourhood). That is the RM↔thing relation, a separate question left open as D3 in the 2026-09-10 spec and reserved for E.D.; the group↔member relation decided here does not touch it. extension_mapping cleared 2026-09-25: it held P46_is_composed_of, the inverse of the core predicate, emitted in the same direction (see is_part_of). The target is a RepresentationModelNodeGroup (E73 Information Object); no CRMarchaeo refinement applies. P46i alone is correct.

allowed_connections._note: Source lists the three concrete representation classes one by one rather than the base RepresentationNode, mirroring what is_in_functional_unit had to do: Node.node_type_map is keyed by node_type, so a base-class name would resolve to a single subclass and refuse the others. A group may itself be a member of another group, which keeps the door open for nesting without requiring it.

_dtc_role_note: dtc_role marks an edge as part of the DTC CHAIN — the three edges a provenance walk may traverse. It exists because the classification used to be written twice: by name on the node (s3dgraphy.dtc) and by PREFIX in the client (startsWith('dtc_')). The prefix presumed every future dtc_* edge would be chain, so a dtc_* edge that is CONTEXT — a dtc_annotated_by, say — would have been a corridor on the client and not on the node: two rules with one name. Now the datamodel says it once and both sides read it. An edge WITHOUT dtc_role is context by construction: adding one is a JSON entry, and it is born non-traversable.
_ui_phrase_note: v1.6.22 · `edge_types.<edge>.ui_phrase` = the phrase an interface uses for a menu entry that CREATES a node already linked to an existing one by this edge. Canonical English; the other languages are in datamodel_translations.json → `edge_types.<edge>.ui_phrase_as_source|ui_phrase_as_target` (text per language + validated_<lang>, the form of every other entry), read with s3dgraphy.tools.datamodel_i18n.edge_ui_phrase(edge, direction, lang), which falls back to this English. TWO DIRECTIONS: `as_source` when the NEW node is the edge's source, `as_target` when it is the target. PLACEHOLDERS, both always present: `{node}` = the label of the new node's TYPE (typeLabel), `{x}` = the NAME of the existing node. Examples: US12 selected, a new US that is more recent — the new US is the source of is_after → as_source «{node} above {x}» → «US above US12»; a new property of US12 — US12 —has_property→ new → as_target «{node} of {x}» → «Property of US12». A SYMMETRIC edge (equals, bonded_to, has_same_time, contrasts_with) has the same phrase both ways. WHICH EDGES: the 34 that EMStudio's menus can propose, MEASURED 2026-10-02 (add-menu.ts linkedItems «Collegato a X» + connectItems, the anchor drag, over the four contexts; probe in .claude/wip/reports/2026-10-02-documento-e-frasi/). The 22 without a phrase are created by an importer, a tool or a structural gesture, never picked from a menu: the alias spellings (is_bonded_to, is_physically_equal_to), the epoch links made by placing a unit in a lane (has_first_epoch, survive_in_epoch) or by the periodisation (has_sub_epoch), the 3D/spatial links written by the tools that make the asset (has_geoposition, has_representation_model*, has_semantic_shape, is_on_resource, has_registration_transform, has_gcp_set, is_in_representation_model_group), validated_by (a person signing a narrative: its own gesture, never a node created from a menu), is_in_functional_unit (the FunctionalUnitNodeGroup is not on EMStudio's authoring surface, add-menu.ts SECTIONS, so no menu reaches it), the HDT-O links written by the twin's own tooling (has_digital_twin, has_digital_twin_component, contains_proposition_set, has_digital_object_part, study_produced_proposition_set), and generic_connection, which is the absence of a relation, not one to propose. The day a menu proposes one of them, it gets its phrase here first (tests/test_edge_ui_phrases.py).
